page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-128 is an ARM-based compute instance built on AmpereOne processors. The configuration provisions 16 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with single-threaded execution (16 vCPUs total), paired with 128 GB of system memory. This yields a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core, positioning the instance within a memory-optimized footprint. It features no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistent disk needs. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent multi-threaded compute and throughput alongside modest single-core execution speed. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng (573.09) and Geekbench single-core (1070.0), place the instance in the lower tier of cloud processors. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics scale reliably across all 16 physical cores, reflected by a stress-ng multi-core score of 9131.57 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9007.0. Memory throughput reaches 101.83 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 72.87 GB/sec for write operations.

Data manipulation and I/O workloads showcase balanced throughput, recording 22.24 million Redis SET operations per second and 23.43 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Software compilation with Clang reaches 19309.0 points in Geekbench. In contrast, instruction sets lack AVX, AVX-512, and AMX extensions, leading to weak throughput in single-threaded LLM inference workloads (67.12 tokens/sec generation on a 135M model and 6.97 tokens/sec on a 7B model).

Given the high memory-per-core density and single-thread tradeoffs, this instance provides cost-efficient operational characteristics for distributed memory caching, web serving fleets, microservice backends, Clang-based CI/CD builds, and relational database hosting where massive memory capacity outweighs single-thread peak performance.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-128 is an ARM64 memory-optimized instance featuring 16 dedicated physical cores (16 vCPUs) on AmpereOne processors clocked at 3.0 GHz, coupled with 128 GB of RAM. The instance allocates 8.0 GB of memory per core and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, but provides no integrated local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations highlight moderate multi-threaded capacity—such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 9007.0 and 22.24 million Redis SET operations per second—contrasted with weak single-core execution speeds and low LLM inference rates due to the absence of advanced vector extensions. Delivering balanced resource density and reliable core isolation, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.8-128 is well suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, CI/CD compilation workloads, and database engines requiring large memory footprints without intense single-thread computational overhead.
